findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the intent-journal recovery contract (journal lifecycle, the three crash-state discriminations, and the SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT-has-no-journal invariant shared across compact_txn/_union_merge/push_recovery/fsck/doctor) in an ADR or design-doc so the boundary survives future edits.
evidence: "Discrimination of the two half-fold states is by an INTENT JOURNAL (a commit-pending sentinel)"
"the retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state has NO journal by construction, so the preamble never touches it — `fsck --repair-snapshots` remains its sole owner"
ABSENCE: no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc artifact is named to capture this novel recovery contract shared by compact_txn, _union_merge, push_recovery, fsck, and doctor.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel architectural pattern — the INTENT JOURNAL / commit-pending sentinel stored outside the worktree under the tracker's git dir — whose recovery semantics are shared and coordinated across five components (compact_txn fold, sync._union_merge reconverge, push_recovery, fsck detection, doctor --repair). This is a new cross-component contract for crash-recovery discrimination (live-journal-uncommitted vs journal-in-HEAD vs SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT-with-no-journal). The plan specifies the mechanism in detail but names no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update to capture the decision, so the invariant 'the retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state has NO journal by construction, so the preamble never touches it' lives only in the child ticket prose and risks being violated by a future edit to any of the five touchpoints.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Crash-atomic compaction fold' (INTENT JOURNAL description)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the untrack-markers commit propagates across the shared store (reconverge/push behavior + the ~89 peer worktrees still tracking markers) and how marker writes during that window are handled, so the migration converges without a peer re-seeding the tracked-marker class.
evidence: Plan: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers (`*/.archived`, `*/.write.lock`) from the tickets branch via an idempotent ensure unit'

RCA context on 6ccc/e72e: '~90 .tickets-tracker dirs are separate worktrees sharing one .git' and 'the shared tracker is being actively written by other sessions right now' — the untrack commit lands into a store under concurrent multi-session write
ABSENCE: the plan states idempotence and reader self-heal but is silent on how the untrack commit reconverges/pushes and how peers that still have markers tracked behave until they reconverge
findings.finding: The 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers' migration (`git rm --cached '*/.archived' '*/.write.lock'` on the shared tickets branch) does not specify how the untrack commit propagates to origin and the ~89 other worktrees that still track the markers in HEAD, nor how marker writes during that propagation window are handled — a dual-write window on a concurrently-written store.
findings.location: Child decomposition: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers'; AC-3
scenarios: The untrack commit is created on worktree A; before it reaches origin/other worktrees, session B (on an un-migrated worktree) closes a ticket, re-committing a tracked `.archived`/`.write.lock`, re-seeding the tracked-dirt class the migration is meant to eliminate
The untrack commit's push races a peer and must reconverge; the ensure unit's interaction with `_union_merge`/push-recovery is unspecified

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the back-out path for the untrack-markers migration and assert the store's coherent state after a revert or partial failure (mixed tracked/untracked markers), not merely that the ensure unit is idempotent on re-apply.
evidence: Plan: '…via an idempotent ensure unit, and make the reader self-heal a missing marker cache'
POST-ROLLBACK applicability: this child narrows/changes interpretation of existing persisted marker records (tracked -> gitignored runtime artifacts)
ABSENCE: no back-out path or post-rollback-state assertion for the untrack commit; AC-3 asserts only the post-apply state (`git ls-files` empty)
findings.finding: The untrack-markers migration changes how existing tracked marker records are interpreted (and pairs with a read-path change to self-heal a missing marker cache) but does not assert the store's state AFTER a back-out of the untrack commit — only that the ensure unit is idempotent when applied.
findings.location: Child decomposition: 'Untrack per-ticket runtime markers'; AC-3
scenarios: An operator or auto-revert backs out the untrack commit; markers become tracked in HEAD again while the reader now expects to self-heal a missing cache — the plan never states whether readers/compaction behave correctly in that reverted state
A partial-failure mid-migration leaves some ticket dirs untracked and others still tracked; the plan does not define the coherent recovery/back-out target

evidence: Plan: journal written 'OUTSIDE the worktree (under the tracker's git dir, so the sentinel itself can never be tree dirt)'
sync.py:253 _quarantine_untracked explicitly uses `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` for exactly the 'outside any working tree' placement, showing the distinction is load-bearing in this codebase
ABSENCE: the plan does not pin common-dir vs per-worktree git-dir for the journal path
findings.finding: The intent-journal location is specified only as 'OUTSIDE the worktree (under the tracker's git dir)', which is ambiguous between the per-worktree git-dir and the common git-dir. The sibling untracked-quarantine code deliberately resolves `--git-common-dir` (sync.py:253); if the fold-writer and the crash-recovery preamble resolve the git dir differently in a linked-worktree tracker, the preamble can miss a live journal and skip the revert it exists to perform.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Crash-atomic compaction fold', intent-journal description
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the journal path relative to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (as sync.py:253 already does for the reconverge quarantine), so both writer and recovery preamble resolve the identical location under any worktree layout.
